newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares outperformed MSCI index in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares outperformed MSCI index in Q1 1997.

text.p: Dutch shares listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange outperformed the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) world re-investment index during the first quarter of 1997, the Dutch Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Wednesday.
Dutch shares gained an average of 15 percent while the MSCI index lagged with an increase of only ten percent during the first quarter.
On March 11, Dutch shares reached a peak with prices an average of 19 percent above end-1996 levels.
High-tech stocks were notable in performing well.

The CBS/Wesselius MITS re-investment index, which includes the shares of all major Dutch micro-electronics, information-technology and telecommunications companies except for heavyweights KPN and Philips, rose by 40 percent during the first quarter of 1997.
Small capitalisation stocks outperformed blue-chips during the first quarter of 1997, the CBS said.
While the AEX-index of the 25 most actively traded stocks rose 14 percent, the CBS/NIBS rating index for small and mid-cap companies gained 22 percent during the first quarter.
The increased level of interest rates in the second half of the first quarter compensated for the lower interest level during the first part of the period.
This resulted in broadly unchanged bond and interest rate levels and a return on bonds of one percent during the first quarter of 1997.
On the first day of the second quarter of 1997, Dutch shares shed 3.9 percent in a reaction to heavy losses on Wall Street on the previous two trading days.
